author: kimothy
body:
Hi @protesilaos. First of all. Thanks for the excellent work on the denote package. I use it every day and I really appreciate the work you have put into it.

I would like to propose an additional function to denote.el, named denote-org-capture-with-defaults. It very similar to the denote-org-capture-with-prompts, but instead of constructing a minibuffer prompt for each non-nil argument, it produces one for each nil argument instead. In addition, the arguments that are passed, are used as passed.

This is practical with the org-mode-capture when you want to limit the the user input. For example, if you have org-capture for a journal entry, you might want to default the subdirectory, tags, title and so on, and prompt the user only for what might differ for the template.

A minimal example of use:

```
(setq denote-org-capture-specifiers "%?")

(setq denote-templates
      '((journal . "* Entry\n")))

(with-eval-after-load 'org-capture
  (add-to-list 'org-capture-templates
      '("j" "Journal Entry" plain
        (file denote-last-path)
        (function (lambda () (denote-org-capture-with-defaults "My Journal Entry" '("journal" "entry") "journal-subdir" nil (alist-get 'journal denote-templates))))
        :no-save t
        :immediate-finish nil
        :kill-buffer t
        :jump-to-captured t)))
```

This specific example captures a note with a specific title, a specific set of tags, into a specific subdirectory using todays date, and with a specific template. The user does not need to be prompted in this case, and the capture buffer will open immediately.

An other example of a org-capture template might be:
```
(setq denote-templates
      '((journal . "* TODO \n")))

(with-eval-after-load 'org-capture
  (add-to-list 'org-capture-templates
      '("t" "Todo" plain
        (file denote-last-path)
        (function (lambda () (denote-org-capture-with-defaults nil '("task") "todo-subdir" nil (alist-get 'todo denote-templates))))
        :no-save t
        :immediate-finish nil
        :kill-buffer t
        :jump-to-captured t)))
```
This would prompt the user for a title, but default the tags, subdir, date, template template is defaulted, which makes it very efficient.

Let me know if you have any comments. Thanks a lot.

author: portsmouth
body: This PR adds a detailed discussion to the spec of the coat darkening effect (incorporating the ideas discussed in https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenPBR/issues/136 and https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenPBR/issues/141), with: - introduction of a new `coat_darkening` parameter (defaulting to 1, the physically correct case). - a physical definition of how this parameter operates to reduce the darkening (via boosting of the base albedo) - a suggested practical implementation of the darkening factor for the base lobe, taking into account the IOR of the coat, and also the roughness of the base (based on the derivations and discussions linked elsewhere). - A suggested implementation of the darkening of colored coats at grazing angles due to longer path length in the absorbing medium. I also include a placeholder for a discussion of how the coat roughness should affect the underlying lobes. (Probably to be done in a separate PR, and derivation of a reasonable physical approximation for this is WIP). To make it easier to read, I broke the Coat section into sub-sections. ![image](https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenPBR/assets/2774364/10c03bcb-0834-45a4-9a6c-8063db8610e5) ![image](https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenPBR/assets/2774364/baaf5f4a-83a5-40d0-a200-16e14079689a) ![image](https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenPBR/assets/2774364/6e3db2ad-f816-4f93-b9ec-06c6da7b62be) ![image](https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenPBR/assets/2774364/6b2c327c-9932-441a-9c3a-728599d26ad4)

<!-- Replace XXXX with the issue number. Issue will be auto-linked -->
Jira issue: SWATCH-2223

## Description
<!-- Provide a description of this PR.  Try to provide answers to "what", "how",
and "why" -->
AWS has a limitation of 1 usage record an hour for a given resource/subscription/org. If remittances are retried then some will fail since they will be billed for the same hour. To prevent this issue we should consume messages from the billable-usage-hourly-aggregate topic instead of from billable-usage topic.

**Deployment Issue**
When this is deployed there will be an overlap of the old swatch-producer-azure and the new billable-usage-hourly-aggregate consumer are reading the same messages. We need to come up with a strategy for preventing duplicate billing during this time.


## Testing
<!--
When possible, please use commands a developer can directly paste or modify
-->

### Setup
<!-- Add any steps required to set up the test case -->
1. Insert test data:
```
INSERT INTO public.offering VALUES ('BASILISK', 'BASILISK', NULL, 0, 0, 0, 0, 'BASLISK', 'Premium', 'Production', NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL);

INSERT INTO subscription(
    sku, org_id, subscription_id, quantity, start_date, end_date, subscription_number, billing_provider, billing_provider_id, billing_account_id)
    VALUES ('BASILISK', '123', '1234436512', '3', '2021-11-30T05:00:00Z', '2031-01-01T01:10:00Z', 123511, 'aws', '12345;test;test', '1234567891234');
```
1. In 3 separate terminals run following commands to start services:

`DEV_MODE=true SERVER_PORT=8101 ./gradlew :bootRun`

```
SERVER_PORT=8001 SWATCH_INTERNAL_SUBSCRIPTION_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8000 KSTREAM_BILLABLE_USAGE_AGGREGATION_WINDOW_DURATION=10s KSTREAM_BILLABLE_USAGE_AGGREGATION_GRACE_DURATION=2s ./gradlew :swatch-producer-azure:quarkusDev
```

`./gradlew  :swatch-producer-aws:quarkusDev`

### Steps

1. Produce the following message twice in a row onto platform.rhsm-subscriptions.billlable-usage topic:
`{"org_id":"123","id":null,"billing_provider":"aws","billing_account_id":"1234567891234","snapshot_date":"2024-01-01T01:10:28Z","product_id":"BASILISK","sla":"Premium","usage":null,"uom":"Storage-gibibyte-months","value":42.0}`
2. Wait at least 12 seconds.
3. Produce the message one more time to the topic (this triggers the previous hourly aggregate message to send)

### Verification

Multiple smaller issues in one PR, what could got wrong?!

[RGT-99] forest tiles
Forest tiles now have correct movement functionality
- Cavalry units cannot move through forest tiles
- Non-cavalry units can move through forests, but only 1 tile at a time
Attack range is not affected by forest tiles

 [RGT-96] Between level inventory menu
 Inventory menu now only functional after a level is completed
 - After a level, the inventory screen is shown as it does now, allowing the player to swap items from units to their inventory
 - During normal gameplay, you can view the inventory and units but cannot swap items back and forth
 
 [RGT-83] QOL for UnitActionMenu
 Unit Action Menu Quality of life features
 - When a unit has moved, and there is no action they can take, they are automatically made to wait
 - When a unit has moved but has other actions besides wait they could take, [A] or [SPACE] now opens the action menu instead of trying to move the units that have no movement left. 
 
 [RGT-89] Ranged Units for AI
 Refactored AI code to work for both melee and ranged units
 - AI can now spawn RangedUnit's, and will attack with the same range as a player version of the same unit
 - Currently no visual indicator for where the unit can attack
 
[RGT-102] HP as level up option
Added HP as an option when prompted to level up a unit
- Ranges from 4-6, as apposed to 1-4 for the normal options
 
 KNOWN ISSUES
~~AI seems to not be able to attack at all, the game hitches when AI is about to move, and the path line stays on screen after the AI, has moved. This most likely has to do with the new level system but I'm not entirely sure, will be looking into this as the main focus for the rest of the playtesting build.~~
Fixed as part of the RangedUnit for AI big overhaul

Furthermore the caller can call the client object's `subscribe` method to get notified of updates.

Thanks for submitting a pull request! Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. Additionally, make sure you've done all of these things:

## PR Description

**What type of PR is this? (Check one of the boxes below)**

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Improvement (non-breaking change which does not add functionality nor fixes a bug but improves Natron in some way)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation
    - [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly

**What does this pull request do?**

- Adds logic to the "Build Installer" GitHub action that verifies that the plugins that are built are actually loadable. This is intended to catch missing dependencies.
- Added missing libheif dependencies that were preventing the Arena and IO plugins from loading.


**Have you tested your changes (if applicable)? If so, how?**

Yes. I tested that the new logic properly detects that the plugins were not loadable and causes the build to fail (https://github.com/acolwell/Natron/actions/runs/7935008735). I then added the missing dependencies and verified that the build started passing again (https://github.com/acolwell/Natron/actions/runs/7935721812).

**Futher details of this pull request**

I'm not exactly sure when libheif took on the new dependencies, but I do know my nightly builds were passing even though the plugins had missing dependencies. This change is intended to make it easier to detect when these new dependencies sneak in and break plugin loading.

body: ### Stories/Links: DOP-4385 ### Notes: * This change allows the preview plugin to consume either Netlify build hook payloads or Gatsby Cloud webhook bodies, depending on where the job is coming from. Netlify's hooks leverage env variables, so we have to parse them accordingly, whereas Gatsby Cloud's are built-in as part of Gatsby's existing `webhookBody` field. * This change should not negatively impact Gatsby Cloud builds. The following build logs show that Gatsby Cloud builds still consume webhook data as expected: * [From a call to the webhook](https://www.gatsbyjs.com/dashboard/083213ad-92d8-4d3f-af78-848bb8100c91/sites/415d6555-c510-4289-a4f2-8593e1b97ee7/builds/c535dee9-9453-44af-95ce-5173e39bb615/details?returnTo=%2Fdashboard%2F083213ad-92d8-4d3f-af78-848bb8100c91%2Fsites%2F415d6555-c510-4289-a4f2-8593e1b97ee7%2FcmsPreview#rawLogs) - see `currentWebhookBody` has custom data passed in. * [From a manual rebuild](https://www.gatsbyjs.com/dashboard/083213ad-92d8-4d3f-af78-848bb8100c91/sites/415d6555-c510-4289-a4f2-8593e1b97ee7/builds/f65771dd-25cd-4582-ab00-1a0c8bdb755b/details?returnTo=%2Fdashboard%2F083213ad-92d8-4d3f-af78-848bb8100c91%2Fsites%2F415d6555-c510-4289-a4f2-8593e1b97ee7%2FcmsPreview#rawLogs) - see `currentWebhookBody` is still `{}` by default. * Please see screenshots below to see Netlify build logs with successful webhook bodies. **Custom payload using Netlify build hook:** **Empty payload through a manual Netlify rebuild:** ### README updates - - [ ] This PR introduces changes that should be reflected in the README, and I have made those updates. - - [x] This PR does not introduce changes that should be reflected in the README

author: jens1608
body:
Awesome job mill1000!
It works flawlessly on my setup :)

I ran into some small problem in my setup:
I'm using active speakers for a multi room setup.
SnapCast-Server -> SnapCast Client on Raspberry Pi Zero -> raspdif -> LED -> Toslink to my speakers.
My speakers are able to automatically activate on Toslink signal and deactivate themselves after 10s without signal.
BUT no signal means Toslink being turned off completely.
I realized in standard configuration, even with "no-keep-alive" the output never turns off, so my speakers are never going to sleep.

I've added a few lines to turn of PCM completely during buffer underrun, this solves my issue and my speakers are going to sleep.
Maybe this might help somebody else with a similar setup.

Thanks again for your amazing work, I really appreciate it!

Regards
Jens

author: sferra
body:
Some metadata providers like Discogs provide track names which include trailing spaces which caused the search to fail. Removing leading and trailing spaces from track and artist names allows us to find any previously missed matches.

To reproduce the issue:
* setup:
  * metadata provider: Discogs
  * stream provider: Bandcamp
* search for "somali sun", select "The Sun" by "Somali Yacht Club"
* no streams on Bandcamp match because all tracks contain trailing spaces and the matching is too strict

author: lunderberg
body:
* Handle non-bundled parameters in LazyTransformParams.

* Check for `"num_input"` attribute

* Handle relax.Const in LazyTransformParams

  Prior to this commit, `LazyTransformParams` would only output a call to the `fset_item` function if that element of the output had a corresponding `relax.Binding`.  If `relax.Const` appeared in the output, then the call to `fset_item` would be omitted.

  This commit updates `LazyTransformParams` to check for any non-`Var` elements of the output tuple.

author: schahal
body:
After some private feedback (and I tend to agree), we want to _remove_ the `uppercase` transformation on secret property keys.

As the rest of the engines (`plaintext` and `kms`) are in abundant use, changing that would be BREAKING. 

I feel we can switch the `sealed` engine template only, as adoption of that is nil (and IMO a breaking change later for the rest of the secret engines).

I think the advantage of letting user explicitly set the key name (rather than doing a "behind-the-scenes" transformation) outweigh the cons (less friction finding/debugging secrets, some 3rd-party charts may require user to have a secret with a specifically styled key, etc)

author: hoebbelsb
body:
# Description

Sorry for delivering multiple things within a single PR...

This PR introduces the following new features:

* appendOnly mode
* initialScrollIndex input

as well as a bugfix for the virtual list template manager that sometimes produced bad diffs and a fix for a viewglitch caused by a mispositioned sentinel.

## AppendOnly

There is a new input `appendOnly: boolean` on the scroll strategies. Enabling this mode causes the rendered range to only increase - in any direction. See https://material.angular.io/cdk/scrolling/overview#append-only-mode

I hope this addresses https://github.com/rx-angular/rx-angular/issues/1686

##  InitialScrollIndex

There is a new input `initialScrollIndex: number` on the `RxVirtualScrollViewportComponent` which lets users define an initial index to scroll to. fixes https://github.com/rx-angular/rx-angular/issues/1689

> the virtual-scroll-viewport now accepts an index as input which sets the first view to be visible to the user. The viewport waits for the data to arrive and scrolls to the given index immediately.

## Bugfix

Fixes https://github.com/rx-angular/rx-angular/issues/1679

I've recorded the following demo ( I did move the logic from the demo stackblitz to our demo repo for this purpose )

author: nick-mon1
body:
## Summary
Current `youtube` shortcode offers no option to set the start time for an embedded youtube video.

Why? Some videos from the [accessibility-for-teams](https://github.com/GSA/digitalgov.gov/pull/7279) guide migration use specific start times to accompany text content.
It would be useful to keep these video bookmarks after the migration and it will also provide the functionality in the future if needed.

### Preview

[Link to Preview](https://federalist-466b7d92-5da1-4208-974f-d61fd4348571.sites.pages.cloud.gov/preview/gsa/digitalgov.gov/nl-refactor-youtube-shortcode/event/2018/09/27/a-conversation-with-evan-papp/)

### Solution

This enhancement adds two fields for setting the required `id` and optional `time`.

**Before**

```
{{< youtube Hvo7WVKvPGU >}}
```

**After**
```
{{< youtube id="Hvo7WVKvPGU" title="Youtube video title" start_time="101" >}}
```

The `title` field sets the html `title` attribute on the `iframe` to meet accessibility.


### Checklist

- [x] updated shortcode partial
- [x] updated existing shortcode instances
- [x] documented enhancements in code
- [ ] updated wiki


### How To Test

1. Visit [page with youtube embed](https://federalist-466b7d92-5da1-4208-974f-d61fd4348571.sites.pages.cloud.gov/preview/gsa/digitalgov.gov/nl-refactor-youtube-shortcode/event/2018/09/27/a-conversation-with-evan-papp/) (the second video on the page)
2. Add `start_time` to shortcode on local build
3. Visit page, press play and video should start at provided time

---

- [x] A11y testing (voice over testing, meets WCAG, run axe tools)
